chapters.title: Chapter 6: Capstone: From Backtest to Live Trading

lessons.title: Putting It Together: A Cost and Slippage Audit Framework

children.text: Chapter 5's checklist told you what to check. This lesson turns that into a process: five ordered steps that take any new strategy candidate from raw backtest to a single, defensible go or no-go decision, producing a one-page audit record you can compare across every strategy your desk considers.

events.title: Classify the Strategy
events.description: Segment (delivery, intraday, futures, options), universe and its typical liquidity tier, and average holding period or turnover ratio.

events.title: Price the Full Cost Stack
events.description: Blended round-trip cost from Chapters 2 and 3: explicit charges, spread, and market impact, calibrated to the strategy's actual segment and liquidity tier.

events.title: Compute Cost Drag and Break-Even
events.description: Cost Drag = Turnover x Round-Trip Cost, from Chapter 4, giving the minimum gross CAGR the strategy must clear.

events.title: Verify Methodology Integrity
events.description: Run the Chapter 5 checklist's fourth category: fill timing, look-ahead bias, and index membership, flagging anything that inflates the gross number itself.

events.title: Apply Margin and Decide
events.description: Compare actual gross CAGR against break-even with a 2x to 3x margin, factor in the Chapter 6 residual-gap buffer, and record a Go or No-Go decision.

children.text: Each of the five steps produces one or two numbers. Recorded together, they form a scorecard, a standard, comparable output for any strategy this framework is run against.
Worked Application: Auditing a New Strategy in One Pass

A quality-value composite strategy, a 25-stock portfolio drawn from the Nifty 500 and rebalanced fortnightly, has not appeared anywhere else in this course. Running it through the five-step process end to end shows the framework working on something genuinely new.

Step 1: Equity delivery, Nifty 500 (a mixed large and mid-cap liquidity tier), roughly 15% of the portfolio replaced per fortnight, 26 fortnights a year, giving a turnover ratio of 3.9x. Step 2: a blended round-trip cost of 0.25%, between the tighter 0.20% used for Nifty 50-only strategies and the 0.30% used for broader midcap-inclusive ones. Step 3: cost drag of 3.9 x 0.25% = 0.975%, the break-even gross CAGR. Step 4: the backtest passes methodology review, fills are next-session, index membership is historically accurate, no flags. Step 5: the backtest's actual gross CAGR is 15.5%.

body.caption: Completed audit scorecard: quality-value composite, Nifty 500, fortnightly

cells: Go, standard probation period per Chapter 6, Lesson 1

stats.label: Safety margin
stats.context: Well above the 2x to 3x guideline from Chapter 4

body.text: A 15.9x safety margin is comfortable enough to absorb even a fairly large calibration error, unlike the daily rebalance strategy from Chapter 4's case study, which cleared break-even at only 1.6x. The audit process does not just produce a yes or no, it produces a number for how confident that answer should be.

children.text: Using the Framework as a Repeatable Process

Run these five steps on every new strategy candidate, not just the ones that feel risky, and keep every completed scorecard. Over time this produces something more valuable than any single audit: a comparable record across every strategy a desk has evaluated, making it possible to see which kinds of strategies consistently clear the bar and which kinds consistently do not, long before that pattern would otherwise become visible.

body.title: Quick Check
body.prompt: Running the five-step framework on a new strategy gives a turnover ratio of 5.0x and a blended round-trip cost of 0.20%. What is its break-even gross CAGR (Step 3), in percent?
body.explanation: Cost Drag = Turnover x Round-Trip Cost = 5.0 x 0.20% = 1.00%. This is the minimum gross CAGR the strategy must clear at Step 3, before Step 5 applies a safety margin on top of it.

body.text: A single formula or checklist item is easy to skip under time pressure. A five-step process that ends in a recorded scorecard is not, because skipping a step leaves a visible gap in the record. This framework's value is less about any one calculation and more about making the whole evaluation repeatable, comparable, and impossible to quietly shortcut.

points: The five-step audit process, classify, price the cost stack, compute break-even, verify methodology, apply margin and decide, turns this course's tools into a repeatable procedure rather than a one-off calculation.
Each step produces a field for a standard audit scorecard, allowing strategies to be compared on the same basis rather than judged inconsistently one at a time.

Applied to a new strategy not seen elsewhere in this course, a Nifty 500 quality-value composite, the framework produced a clear Go decision with a 15.9x safety margin, in the same five steps used throughout.
Keeping every completed scorecard builds a comparable record across strategies over time, turning individual audits into an institutional memory of what tends to work and what does not.
